For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.

title: On quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimensions
abstract: Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.

title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
abstract: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.

title: Sharp box-dimension bounds for fractional integrals under unequal Hölder and anti-Hölder exponents
abstract: Let $0<h\le H<1$ and $0<σ<1$. Graph box dimensions are studied for fractional integrals of functions satisfying an $h$-Holder upper bound on increments and an $H$-anti-H lder lower bound on oscillation on a nondegenerate subinterval. For the Riemann--Liouville integral, the following inequalities hold: \[ \begin{aligned} \max\{1,2-H-σH/h\} &\le\lbdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1])\\ &\le\ubdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1]) \le\max\{1,2-h-σ\}. \end{aligned} \] The lower bound is obtained by balancing the truncation error of a Marchaud inverse against the oscillation of the input. For each $(h,H)$, a single sparse tent construction attains it for all $σ\in(0,1)$. The same bounds and their optimality are established for Hadamard integrals on compact intervals bounded away from zero and for left- and right-sided Liouville--Weyl integrals under explicit weighted tail conditions. Zero-mean periodic Weyl integrals with conditionally convergent tails are treated separately. For Hadamard integrals the bounds are transferred by a bi-Lipschitz logarithmic change of variables. For Weyl integrals the transfer relies on invariance of graph box dimensions under continuous perturbations of bounded variation. Local hypotheses and point-dependent anti-Hölder constants are also treated. The exact linear dimension law is recovered for equal exponents, whereas unequal exponents allow a strictly greater loss of graph dimension.

title: Collineations of the diamond lattice in a Hilbert space
abstract: Let $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$ such that $\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}=\{0\}$ and $\mathscr{M}+\mathscr{N}$ is dense in $\mathscr{H}$. We characterize when there exists an invertible operator on $\mathscr{H}$ which maps $\mathscr{M}$ onto $\mathscr{N}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ onto $\mathscr{M}$. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators $(I-P)Q$ and $(I-Q)P$ is compact, or $P-Q$ is compact and $\dim(\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}^\perp)=\dim(\mathscr{M}^\perp\cap\mathscr{N})$, where $P$ and $Q$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice $\{\{0\},\mathscr{M},\mathscr{N},\mathscr{H}\}$ which fix $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.

title: On the Type E case of the Brown Wemyss realization conjecture
abstract: We consider the remaining Type E case of the Brown-Wemyss numerical realization conjecture. The noncommutative splitting lemma and the Type A and D classifications of Brown and Wemyss leave two-generator cyclic potentials with cubic part $x^3$. For these remaining potentials, we construct geometric realizations under the hypothesis of radical growth dimension at most one. The construction combines marked ADE deformations and cyclic coordinate changes for lengths three, four, and six with a filtered finiteness argument in length five. Under the numerical growth hypothesis, cubic lower bounds exclude the other branches for every choice of formal tail. The resulting contractions have a regular source and a complete local cDV target. Finite-dimensional algebras are realized by threefold flops, and the sole growth-one algebra in this residual case is $\operatorname{Jac}(x^3+xy^3)$, for which we give a divisor-to-curve contraction.

title: Distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
abstract: The gem is obtained by joining a vertex to every vertex of a path on four vertices. A distance-hereditary split graph is a split graph containing no induced gem. In this paper, we characterize all connected distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1 and determine the multiplicity of the eigenvalue 1. Our result extends previous results on threshold graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1.

title: Fixed-opening-set positivity for perfect matchings
abstract: For a perfect matching $M$ on $[2n]$, let $P_M$ be the interval order on its edges and let $\operatorname{Open}(M)$ be the set of smaller endpoints of its edges. For an opening set $O$ that occurs for some matching, put $S_O=\sum_{\operatorname{Open}(M)=O}X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P_M)}$ and $H_O=ωS_O$. We give explicit Schur and power-sum expansions of $H_O$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and prove that $H_O$ is $h$-positive (equivalently, $S_O$ is $e$-positive). The Schur coefficients count standard tableaux of staggered skew shapes with prescribed entries in the left cells of distinguished dominoes. The Schur expansion follows from a Jacobi--Trudi sign-reversing involution on arrays with prescribed opener positions. For every partition $μ$ of $n$, a coefficient-transfer formula expresses $[h_μ]H_O$ as a positive scalar multiple of an elementary coefficient of the chromatic symmetric function of a clique blow-up of a path. This graph is a unit interval graph, so Hikita's theorem gives nonnegativity. The power-sum coefficients admit a cycle-type autocorrelation formula in terms of the restricted permutations from the Ferrers threshold model and an interpretation by alternating permutations with prescribed valley values and record partitions; we also obtain explicit threshold formulas. Further results include descent-set refinements, formulas for selected $h$-coefficients, and a rim-hook cancellation for the coefficient of $h_n$. These results refine the global matching identity of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.

title: Stein degree on birational log Calabi-Yau fibrations
abstract: We prove uniform bounds for the Stein degrees of boundary divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations of Fano type over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero. The main ingredient is the birational case for which we provide two approaches.

title: Fourier bases for square-order Paley graphs
abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

title: Positive semidefiniteness of random submatrices
abstract: Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). The key ingredient is a dense model lemma for positive semidefinite matrices, proved using the hyperplane separation theorem and a contraction inequality for Rademacher random variables.

title: Self-Orthogonal MDS Principal-Ideal Codes
abstract: We investigate Euclidean self-orthogonality and the generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) property for coefficient-vector codes generated by a monic polynomial $g$ and its shifts $xg,\ldots,x^{k-1}g$, of length $n=r+k$ and dimension $k$, where $°g=r$ and $3\le k\le r$. We give a complete classification, over any algebraically closed field, of the generators for which these codes are both self-orthogonal and GRS. Such generators have either distinct roots in a geometric progression satisfying explicit order and scalar conditions, or a single repeated root in certain positive characteristics. In particular, only finitely many generators occur for fixed $r$, $k$, and characteristic. We determine their maximal self-orthogonal lengths, show that the corresponding maximal-length codes are cyclic or negacyclic, and obtain exact generator counts over finite fields, together with the least fields of definition. In contrast, when $3\le k<r$, we prove that every algebraically closed field supports infinitely many pairwise monomially inequivalent self-orthogonal non-GRS maximum distance separable (MDS) codes in this family. Consequently, arbitrarily many such codes can be realized over a common finite extension of any prescribed finite field, while remaining inequivalent and non-GRS over its algebraic closure.

title: Material optimization of optical properties of particulate products by transition matrix method and sequential global programming
abstract:
Material optimization of nanoparticle assemblies, such as structurally coloured photonic crystals, attracts increasing interest. We combine the transition matrix method (TMM), which avoids spatial discretization of particles and surrounding medium, with sequential global programming (SGP) to optimize optical properties of particulate products by iteratively assigning predefined catalogue materials to individual particles.
  We derive exact separable models, reproducing the fully coupled objective under single-particle material changes, and computationally accessible first-order correct approximations for general continuously differentiable objectives. These approximations aim to capture the nonlinear, potentially nonconvex dependence on individual material variables beyond their local first-order behaviour. Within SGP, globally minimizing the particle-wise subproblems can yield substantial improvements in few outer iterations, including steps away from unfavourable stationary points, as previously demonstrated for discrete dipole approximation-based SGP. The construction exploits the decomposition of the TMM system matrix into a material-dependent block-diagonal and a material-independent coupling matrix, while the state and adjoint problems remain fully coupled.
  Applications include extinction, scattering quantities, and colour objectives. In a 35-particle extinction minimization problem, the objective decreases by 31.0% in 13 iterations. A fine-grid evaluation of the fully coupled objective shows that no tested single-particle material change improves the final design. For a 627-particle photonic crystal, chroma increases by 58.4-122.1% for different particle diameters in 17-42 iterations. The optimized designs favour absorbing material in layers away from the incident light, consistent with experimental findings.

title: An A $\infty$ -algebra structure for enriched Morse complexes
abstract: We construct a homotopy coherent product structure extending the Chas-Sullivan product on chains of the free loop space of a manifold. Our construction uses the framework of Morse homology with DG coefficients and perturbed Morse gradient trees. We define an operad given by moduli spaces of Morse gradient trees with a twisted differential. This Morse tree operad receives a map from a suspended A$\infty$-operad and in turn acts on Morse homology with DG coefficients associated to a fibration over a manifold with a fibrewise monoidal structure.

title: Finite groups with a fixed-point-free automorphism satisfying an irreducible identity
abstract:
For any given irreducible polynomial $f(x)=a_0+a_1\cdot x+\cdots+a_d\cdot x^d\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, we study the structure of finite groups $(G,\cdot)$ that have a fixed-point-free-automorphism $α$ satisfying the condition \[
  \{g^{a_0}\cdotα(g)^{a_1}\cdotsα^d(g)^{a_d}\mid g\in G\}=\{1\}. \] We show that such a group $G$ is nilpotent of class at most $d^{2^d}$, provided that $|G|$ is coprime to an explicit, non-zero, integer invariant $ι(f(x))$ of $f(x)$. We do this by extending the solutions of the Frobenius conjecture. We also extend the solution of the restricted Burnside problem in prime exponent and the classification of the $n$-abelian groups.

title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
abstract: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.

title: Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$
abstract: Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(γ>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ γ=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.

title: Taylor expansions for first-passage time distributions of Brownian motion with moving boundaries
abstract: We analyse the distribution of the first-passage time of Brownian motion to a time-dependent boundary as a function of the boundary. We prove that the boundary-to-distribution map is infinitely many times differentiable along the Cameron-Martin space $\mathscr{H},$ and obtain a with a bound on the truncation error Taylor expansion with a bound on the truncation error. We obtain identities connecting (i) the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution, (ii) the Wiener-Itô chaos kernels of the indicator that the Brownian motion stays below the boundary, and (iii) Krylov-Veretennikov-Zvonkin-type operators. These identities yield relatively tractable representations for the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution when the taboo transition density is available, notably for linear boundaries. As an application of the above results we propose Taylor approximations up to second order of the first-passage time distribution. In the examples considered, the first-order approximation is more accurate than the classical tangent approximation and its hazard-rate variant, while remaining straightforward to implement.

title: Wolff-type ideal theorems for slice regular functions
abstract: We study Wolff-type ideal problems in $H^\infty(\mathbb B)$, the algebra of bounded slice regular functions on the quaternionic unit ball. We construct $f,f_1,f_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|f|^2\le |f_1|^2+|f_2|^2$ such that $f^{\ast N}\notin\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ for every integer $N\ge1$, where $\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ denotes the right ideal generated by $f_1$ and $f_2$. We also construct intrinsic functions $a,a_1,a_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|a|\le |a_1|+|a_2|\le1$ and $a^{\ast2}\notin\mathcal I(a_1,a_2)$. For intrinsic data satisfying $|f|\le\sum_{\ell=1}^n|f_\ell|$, the cube $f^{\ast3}$ has a representation in the generated right ideal with intrinsic coefficients. For general data, we obtain sufficient conditions for ideal membership under a fourth-order pointwise bound with a Dini factor. If the generators preserve a common slice, a quadratic bound with a Dini factor suffices.

title: A Faà di Bruno Convolution Identity in Parafermion Operator Products
abstract: We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.

title: Geodesics for generalised complex Hessian equations
abstract: We study geodesics associated with a class of generalized complex Hessian equations on compact Kähler manifolds. The defining polynomial is allowed to have degree \(1\leq d\leq n\) and is assumed to be right-Noetherian. We establish the existence of unique smooth solutions to an elliptic regularization of the geodesic equation and derive uniform a priori estimates, independent of the regularization parameter. A key ingredient is a partial Legendre transform, which reduces the regularized equation to a form that allows us to obtain uniform spatial and mixed Hessian estimates. These estimates yield the existence of unique weak geodesics as limits of the regularized solutions, with convergence in \(C^{1,α}\) for every \(0<α<1\). We further establish convexity properties of associated functionals: the \(I_2\)-functional is affine and the \(J_1\)-functional is convex along weak geodesics. Finally, we study the induced \(\mathcal{E}^{p}\)-Finsler geometry on the space of admissible potentials and prove that the lengths of the regularized geodesics converge to the corresponding path distances, the \(\mathcal{E}^{p}\)-energies of the regularized geodesics converge uniformly in time to the \(p\)-th power of the corresponding path distance, and that the resulting path distance is a genuine metric for every \(1\leq p<\infty\).

title: Determinant Massey products
abstract: We introduce the determinant Massey product, a secondary operation on the cohomology of commutative dg algebras which is reminiscent of the classical Massey product. We prove some of the elementary properties of this product, compute several examples, and relate them to classical and matric Massey products. When 2 is invertible, a determinant Massey product is a matric Massey product, but over $\mathbb F_2$, it is not. In this case, we produce a finite-dimensional cdga whose Harrison cohomology does not inject into its Hochschild cohomology, and a divided powers algebra which is formal as an associative dg algebra, but not as a commutative one, with an explicit determinant Massey product witnessing the failure. Over $\mathbb Q$, we use determinant Massey products to construct a simply-connected coformal space with Koszul cohomology ring and vanishing ordinary Massey products of all orders, which is not formal.

title: Linear dependence and tameness for homogeneous nilpotent-Jacobian maps in dimension four
abstract: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $H\in K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]^4$ be homogeneous of positive degree. We prove that the components of $H$ are linearly dependent over $K$ whenever $JH$ is nilpotent, extending the known quadratic and cubic results to every positive homogeneous degree. This fills the gap regarding homogeneous linear dependence in four dimensions. The proof combines the nilpotent flag with the geometry of the geometric generic affine fibers and the projective image surface. Line fibers are treated by homogeneous quasi-translations. For nonlinear fibers, three successive invariants constrain the directions at infinity, reducing the nonplanar image to a developable surface or a smooth quadric. Boundary, ruling, and trace identities exclude both alternatives. We further prove that $X+H$ is one-stably tame in every degree and tame in four variables through degree five.

title: Depth of Powers of Cover Ideals of Path Ideals
abstract: Let $ J_t(P_n) = (x_1, \ldots, x_t) \cap \cdots \cap (x_{n-t+1}, \ldots, x_n) $ be the cover ideal of the $t$-path ideal of a path graph inside the polynomial ring $ S = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n] $ over a field $K$. For every $ n \ge t \ge 2 $ and $s \ge 2$, we prove that \[ \operatorname{depth} \left ( S/J_t(P_n)^s \right ) = q(s+1) + \left\lfloor \frac{r-1}{t} \right\rfloor, \] where $ n = q(ts + 1) + r $ with $ 1 \le r \le ts + 1 $. Our proof shows that all powers of $J_t(P_n)$ have linear quotients in increasing lexicographic order and explicitly describes the corresponding colon ideals.

title: Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold
abstract:
We construct a global solution to the confined Vlasov--Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium that exhibits infinite-time growth driven by nonlinear plasma echoes. For every sufficiently small \(ε>0\), the initial perturbation has size \(O(ε)\) in a Gevrey-3 norm with radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\). The corresponding solution is real and neutral, and the full distribution remains nonnegative. Its kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology, while the spatial density and electric field decay. Nevertheless, the kinetic profile satisfies
  \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|f(t)\|_{H^{1000}_{z,v}}=\infty. \]
  The construction combines infinitely many well-separated echo cascades within a single global nonlinear solution. Each cascade generates a high-frequency output that persists under the subsequent evolution, and the accumulated outputs produce divergence in a fixed Sobolev norm. Thus, unlike finite-time echo amplification, the instability persists to arbitrarily large times despite scattering and macroscopic Landau damping. The construction identifies an instability mechanism at the critical amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\), where cumulative echo amplification balances the initial Fourier decay.

title: On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group
abstract: The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.

title: Rational Designs and Prouhet--Tarry--Escott Problems
abstract: For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.

title: Separated solutions for a critical competitive system with sublinear coupling in domains with shrinking holes
abstract: We construct nonnegative, fully nontrivial separated solutions for the critical competitive system of two coupled elliptic equations with a sublinear competitive coupling, in a bounded domain with two shrinking holes, for $N\ge5$ and every fixed $β<0$; each component concentrates at one of the holes and vanishes near the other. The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument. This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.

title: Quantitative approximations for finite-state mean-field configuration models
abstract:
We establish quantitative approximations for the empirical measures of finite-state mean-field particle systems in a general framework. The scales of the empirical drift and covariance distinguish the ODE and critical diffusion regimes and determine the corresponding time rescaling.
  In the ODE regime, we obtain quantitative central limit approximations in the $1$-Wasserstein distance and a Bernstein-type concentration inequality. The concentration bound has no dimensional prefactor. Its explicit time dependence also identifies growing intervals on which the ODE approximation remains accurate. In the critical regime, we prove a quantitative nonlinear diffusion approximation in the $1$-Wasserstein distance. We apply our quantitative approximation results to noisy voter systems, Moran models with mutations and selections, heat-bath Glauber dynamics for the $p$-spin Curie--Weiss model, and autocatalytic reactions with mutations.

title: Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems
abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communications through adaptive antenna repositioning. Recently, Fourier neural operators (FNOs) have shown strong potential for FAS channel estimation owing to their ability to learn resolution-invariant mappings and generalize across different port densities. However, existing operator learning approaches require densely sampled channel realizations as training labels, whereas a practical receiver only collects noisy pilot observations from a small subset of ports. This mismatch between training requirements and practical channel acquisition poses a major obstacle to deployment. To address this challenge, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains the FNO-based estimator directly from noisy sub-sampled pilots without any labeled channel fields. The proposed objective combines a pilot splitting strategy, which creates supervision at ports hidden from the model input, with a correction based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) that eliminates the measurement noise bias. We prove that this objective admits the same minimum mean square error (MMSE) solution as the ideal supervised criterion. Since the loss relies solely on received pilots, the estimator can be continually adapted online on the live pilot stream. Simulation results show that the self-supervised FNO achieves accuracy comparable to supervised training, generalizes zero-shot to unseen port resolutions, and rapidly recovers from distribution shift via online adaptation.

title: Displaceability of monotone Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$
abstract: We show that the generalized Polterovich submanifold $L_{0, 2}^P$ in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and the Chekanov-Oakley-Usher Lagrangian $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ in the quadric $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$ are displaceable. Since $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ are in the zero level set of the moment maps of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-actions on $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$, the main idea is to construct Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms mapping $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ to nonzero level sets of the moment maps.

title: A weakly singular Volterra integral equation and the fractional Lyapunov asymptotic stability theorem
abstract: We study the weakly singular Volterra integral equation V(t) = A - (1/Gamma(alpha)) int_0^t (t-s)^{alpha-1} h(|V(s)|) ds, t >= 0, where alpha in (0,1), A > 0 and h is a class-K function. This equation arises as the scalar reduction of fractional-order Lyapunov inequalities through the fractional variation-of-constants formula. We prove that it admits a unique global solution V with 0 < V(t) <= A, that V is non-increasing, and that V(t) tends to 0 as t goes to infinity, under the pure class-K hypothesis on h. If, in addition, h is locally Holder continuous on (0,infinity) with exponent beta > 1 - alpha, then the rescaled function W(t) := V(t^{1/alpha}) is of class C^1 on [0,infinity) and satisfies W'(t) <= 0. We determine the optimal regularity of the solution, which is alpha-Holder continuous with the sharp expansion V(t) = A - h(A) t^alpha / Gamma(alpha+1) + o(t^alpha) at the origin, and its sharp decay rate h(V(t)) ~ A t^{-alpha} / Gamma(1-alpha) as t goes to infinity. In the power case h(x) ~ kappa x^p one has V(t) ~ (A/(kappa Gamma(1-alpha)))^{1/p} t^{-alpha/p}. As an application, we give a complete proof of the fractional-order Lyapunov asymptotic stability theorem of Li, Chen and Podlubny (Theorem 11, Automatica 45 (2009), 1965-1969) under the general class-K hypothesis, a case not covered by the linear, power-law and convex arguments available in the literature. This theorem plays for fractional-order stability theory the role of Lyapunov's classical theorem for ODEs, and its proof closes a gap that has been open since the theorem first appeared. We further show that the Caputo inequality C_0D_t^alpha V(t) <= -c V^p(t) with 0 < p < 1 implies Mittag-Leffler stability of V, yet neither entails nor precludes finite-time decay to zero, in contrast with the integer-order criterion V'(t) <= -c V^p(t), which entails finite-time decay to zero.

title: Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of smooth solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}$
abstract: We study the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb T^d$ with $d\ge2$. For every $2<q\le\infty$ and every smooth mean-zero background solution $U$, we construct two distinct mild solutions with the same initial datum arbitrarily close to $U(0)$ in $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$, both belonging to $C([0,T];\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)) \cap C^\infty((0,T]\times\mathbb T^d)$. The time $T>0$ depends on the background solution but is independent of the prescribed tolerance for the initial data. This gives non-uniqueness for arbitrarily small initial data and density of non-unique initial data in the mean-zero divergence-free subspace of $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $2<q<\infty$. We also prove uniqueness in the same solution class for $1\le q\le2$, establishing the sharp threshold $q=2$ in this Besov scale. The uniqueness result extends to $\dot B^{-1+d/p}_{p,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $1\le p<\infty$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, under the same continuity and smoothness assumptions.

title: Characterizations and Algebraic, Perturbation, and Topological Properties of $θ(H)$
abstract: Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $θ(H)$ be the class of bounded operators whose restrictions to every nonzero closed reducing subspace attain their numerical radii. We characterize this property by eigenvalues of suitable self-adjoint parts. For normal operators, membership in $θ(H)$ is equivalent to pure point spectrum and reverse well-ordering of the moduli of eigenvalues. Without normality assumptions, we prove stability under finite orthogonal direct sums using graph subspaces of closed, possibly unbounded, intertwining operators. We give a compact-perturbation criterion in terms of the essential numerical radius and show that an operator remains in $θ(H)$ under every compact perturbation if and only if it is compact. Finally, $θ(H)$ is norm-dense in $\mathcal B(H)$ and is norm closed if and only if $H$ is finite-dimensional.

title: Twisted enveloping algebras for permutation orbifolds
abstract:
We formulate a topological formal calculus for continuous distributions with values in linearly topologized spaces.
  We apply it here to construct permutation-twisted fields directly from products and branch specializations.
  For a vertex operator algebra $V$, the key structural observation is that modes of tensors with at most one non-vacuum factor topologically generate the permutation-twisted enveloping algebra.
  Combining this observation with the calculus and $Δ_N$, we obtain
  an explicit isomorphism $\mathscr{U}_σ(V^{\otimes N})\cong\mathscr{U}(V)$
  for an $N$-cycle $σ$, with grading and canonical filtrations rescaled by $N$.
  For arbitrary permutations, the cycle factors are rescaled before taking their degreewise completed tensor product.

title: Computing Optimal Non-stationary Policies for the Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Problems
abstract: We develop and analyze an algorithm for computing optimal non-stationary policies for probabilistic reach-avoid problems. The objective in probabilistic reach-avoid problems is to maximize the probability of reaching a goal without visiting predefined avoid states. Prior work has focused on computing optimal stationary reach-avoid policies. Stationary policies use the same action distribution whenever a given state is visited. This paper shows that stationary reach-avoid policies may be suboptimal and non-stationary policies may outperform them in reach probability by a margin arbitrarily close to one. To compute optimal non-stationary policies, we reduce the reach-avoid problem to a constrained average-reward Markov decision problem and propose an algorithm to compute lottery-based policies from a standard linear program formulation. We prove that the lottery-based policies are optimal and show that they are simple to compute, analyze, interpret, and implement. The numerical experiments confirm that the lottery-based policies can outperform state-of-the-art stationary policies even in complex domains.

title: Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator
abstract:
We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average.
  The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

title: Ordering Is Not Deciding: Towards Preference-Consistent Multi-Objective Design--Decision Optimisation
abstract:
In integrated design and group decision-making, Pareto filtering identifies non-dominated alternatives but does not determine which design best fits actors' preferences. Applying those preferences after filtering does not guarantee that the best-fit solution will be found: the filter may already have excluded the alternative with the highest aggregated preference, even when all combinations of fixed performance-improvement directions are considered.
  We compare Pareto--based selection with Integrative Maximisation of Aggregated Preferences (IMAP) on constructed multi-objective design--decision problems, using identical feasible solution spaces and actor preferences for both methods. The problems involve two system performances and up to four preference functions elicited from up to two actors. They cover independent and interdependent relationships between feasible performance values, monotonic and non-monotonic preference functions, and conflicting preferences for the same performance. In some cases, Pareto filtering excludes the best-fit solution, whereas IMAP identifies it.
  These counterexamples show that Pareto optimality does not guarantee a preference consistent decision, even in problems much simpler than real-world design and group decision-making problems. Pareto analysis can support ordering and exploration in performance space. IMAP instead models and aggregates actor preferences before optimisation and maximises the resulting aggregate preference over the full feasible and acceptable solution space.

title: Microscopic Probabilities for U-Statistics and Almost-Balanced Permutations
abstract:
We estimate the probability that a vector of U-statistics lies within $C/n$ of a target in the range of typical fluctuations. For sufficiently large $C$, we prove a lower bound of the typical Gaussian order under finite variance, and a matching upper bound for bounded kernels. We show that under finite variance alone, stronger concentration may occur, and find the best possible asymptotic upper bound. Our proof is algorithmic, estimating probabilities by counting successful modifications produced by a random algorithm.
  We apply this result to settle a question of Beniamini, Lavee and Linial (2025), who asked if there exist permutations with $k$-order sub-pattern counts at most $O(n^{k-1})$ away from one another for $k>4$. We prove not only existence, but enumerate these permutations up to a constant factor, showing that there are $Θ(n!n^{-(k-1)^2/2})$ such permutations of size $n$.

title: The compressible-incompressible CAO problem introduced by Lions, Temam and Wang
abstract: We study the (CAO) system of Lions-Temam-Wang, describing a compressible atmosphere coupled to an incompressible ocean through a fully nonlinear boundary condition representing wind stress at the interface. In their foundational work, the system is reformulated in pressure coordinates under the assumption that the pressure is constant at the interface, leading to a purely incompressible system. In this article, we prove for the first time the strong well-posedness of the coupled compressible-incompressible system both locally and globally for small initial data.

title: Block decimation and perfect actions for $p$-adic valued path integrals
abstract: In earlier work we introduced a finite-partition propagator for $\mathbb{C}_p$-valued wave functions, in which the intermediate positions are integrated against atomic measures. The iterated integral evaluates the action on the equally spaced chain between the endpoints, so each partition level is obtained by iterating an exact, tree-level block decimation of two-point lattice actions, with no integration over fluctuations. This kinematic decimation is the Fréchet derivative, at the free actions, of the variational decimation underlying classical perfect actions. Since the time step $p^n$ is small in the real norm exactly when it is large $p$-adically, refinement and coarsening (the ultraviolet and infrared directions over $\mathbb{R}$) exchange roles, and each yields one limit. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn integral; with the weight no limit exists. For the harmonic oscillator no refinement limit exists at fixed frequency, but under coarsening the variational flow is solved in closed form: the lattice angle is multiplied by $p$ at each step, the coupling obeys a Chebyshev recursion, no caustic occurs, and the rescaled action converges to a free action with renormalized mass $m_0\sin_p(θ_0)/θ_0$. The rescaled linearized map is diagonalizable on polynomial actions with eigenvalues $p^{2-b}$, so directions relevant over $\mathbb{R}$ are irrelevant over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and conversely.

title: Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle
abstract: This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic solutions of the limiting coupled NLS system, obtaining an approximation uniform for all times in the nonrelativistic regime. By this result, we further show that there exists a positive-measure set of frequencies such that, for each frequency, we can fix a quasi-periodic solution of the coupled NLS system and a suitable subsequence of Klein-Gordon solutions converging globally in time to the fixed NLS solution.

title: Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\)
abstract:
In this paper, we study the following Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\): \[
  \sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N}|u(z)-u(z-e_j)|^2
  -C_H(n,m)\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ}
  \frac{|u(z)|^2}{d_Σ(z)^2}
  \geq\overlineκ_{m,n}\|u\|_{\ell^{2^*}(\mathbb Z^N)}^2,
  \quad u\in C_c(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ), \] where \(n,m\geq1\), \(N=n+m\geq3\), \(Σ=\mathbb Z^n\times\{0\}\), \(2^*=2N/(N-2)\), \(e_j\) is the \(j\)-th coordinate vector, \(d_Σ(z):=\inf_{ζ\inΣ}|z-ζ|\), and \(C_H(n,m)\) is the best constant for the Hardy inequality on \(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ\).
  Using the supersolution method and multilinear interpolation, we first prove that the best constant \(\overlineκ_{m,n}\) is positive if and only if either \(1\leq m\leq8\) and \(n\geq1\), or \(m=9\) and \(n\geq14\). Then, we show that \[
  \overlineκ_{m,n}=\overline S_N
  \quad\text{if }m=2\text{ or }(m,n)=(1,2), \] where \(\overline S_N\) is the best constant in the critical Sobolev inequality on \(D^{1,2}(\mathbb Z^N)\). Moreover, for \(m\neq2\) and \(N\geq4\), we prove \(0\leq\overlineκ_{m,n}<\overline S_N\). Finally, using the equality \(\overlineκ_{2,n}=\overline S_{n+2}\), we prove that \(\overlineκ_{2,n}\) is not attained, while for \((m,n)=(1,2)\), we establish nonattainment of \(\overlineκ_{1,2}\) by developing a duality argument based on a comparison of Green functions.

title: Constructible properties of minimal models
abstract: We prove that, given a projective minimal model and a projective family of good minimal models, the subset of the base parametrizing fibers isomorphic (or birationally equivalent) to the given minimal model is constructible in the Zariski topology. Together with recent boundedness results for polarized log Calabi--Yau fibrations, this constructibility theorem provides new finiteness results predicted by the relative Kawamata--Morrison--Totaro cone conjecture.

title: Extremal spectral results of outerplanar graphs without starlike trees
abstract: A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle. When $l_1=l_2=\cdots=l_t=l$, we abbreviate these graphs as $S(t\cdot l)$ and $C_{t\cdot l}$, respectively. Previous results determined $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(t\cdot l))$ for $t\ge4$ [Graphs Combin. 42 (2026) 80] and for $t=3$, in each case for sufficiently large $n$. For $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$, the corresponding extremal graphs are known for $t=2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The sets $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{t\cdot l})$ were also determined for sufficiently large $n$ [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114673]. In this paper, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t))$ for sufficiently large $n$ when the branch lengths are not all equal. Our result for $t\ge4$ also includes equal branch lengths. As applications, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t})$ for arbitrary cycle lengths and sufficiently large $n$. We also determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ for certain linear forests $F=\bigcup_{i=1}^tP_{l_i}$ and sufficiently large $n$. Finally, we apply our main theorems to obtain the known results on outerplanar graphs forbidding matchings or theta graphs for sufficiently large $n$.

title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
abstract: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.

title: Finitely supported mapping classes on infinite-type surfaces
abstract: We study the topological closure of the group of mapping classes group with finite-type support on an infinite-type surface. Since every such mapping class fixes each end which is not a puncture, we have that the closure is contained in the pointwise stabilizer of infinite-type ends. A natural question is therefore when this inclusion is an equality, and if it is not, what must be added to obtain the full stabilizer. We prove that finitely supported mapping classes are dense in the stabilizer precisely when there is at most one end accumulated by genus and at most one end accumulated by punctures. We show that if we remove either of these conditions, we need to add puncture and/or handle shifts to topologically generate the stabilizer.

title: Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations
abstract: This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincaré-type compactification, but a general theory was not established. Here, the two-dimensional ODE system derived by the linear chain trick is rewritten as an orbit equation, and a comparison theorem and an Osgood-type integral condition are applied to obtain a blow-up criterion based on the existence of a subsolution. This characterizes the nonlinearities for which memory-induced blow-up occurs. This paper also gives a necessary condition in a special case, a global existence condition based on a supersolution, and a systematic method for constructing subsolutions for separable nonlinearities. These results recover the author's previous results and are illustrated through several examples.

title: Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity
abstract: We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.

title: k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
abstract: The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetković in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$. For each fixed $k\geq2$, we also determine the $k$-trees attaining the largest second largest eigenvalue below $1$ and the smallest above $1$. Finally, we determine all minimal forbidden induced subgraphs among $k$-trees with $k\geq 1$, each of which has second largest eigenvalue greater than $1$, but deleting any vertex gives a graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$.

title: Supersymmetric Hilbert complexes and Witten deformation on stratified pseudomanifolds
abstract:
We present a framework to study topics related to index theory and Dirac operators with N=1,2 supersymmetry (SUSY), extending it to stratified pseudomanifolds with wedge metrics (iterated conic metrics). We use this to construct Witten deformed subcomplexes of SUSY Hilbert complexes that categorify Morse polynomials and equivariant index formulae for a large class of operators.
  This allows us to prove equivariant index theorems for spin-c Dirac operators with Hamiltonian actions, and Holomorphic Morse inequalities in the Kähler case, in particular proving a new type of equivariant Riemann-Roch (ERR) theorem on singular spaces. We also improve on stratified Morse-Bott inequalities in the de Rham case, and review other applications including for the Kervaire semi-characteristic and the equivariant signature. We compute local cohomology groups for the Dolbeault complexes at both smooth and singular non-isolated fixed point sets which categorify the ERR numbers.
  In an Appendix joint with Alex R. Taylor, we give a broad overview of the relevance of SUSY to index theory on manifolds with boundaries and singularities, mainly focusing on the new insights and results related to N=2 SUSY that the authors have uncovered recently.

title: Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
abstract: We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calderón--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a deterministic large-scale regularity theory for optimal transport with $p$-costs, based on a harmonic approximation by a non-linear elliptic equation of $p$-Laplacian type, with tail bounds on local matching costs.

title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
abstract: We study positive solutions of the Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + a(t)g(u)=0,\qquad u'(0)=u'(T)=0, \] with a two-step sign-changing weight. Under an explicit condition on an increasing nonlinearity \(g\), we prove that for every prescribed integer \(N\ge 1\) and every prescribed ratio \(κ>0\) of the step lengths, there exist step weights of that ratio and strictly negative integral for which the problem has at least \(N\) distinct positive solutions. The multiplicity persists under small perturbations of the weight parameters. A structural condition on \(g'/g\) yields at least three positive Neumann solutions for \(g(u)=e^{u^p}-1\) for every \(p>1\). An explicit increasing nonlinearity also satisfies the \(N\)-solution criterion for every finite \(N\), with the weight chosen separately in each case.

title: Preconditioning for quadratic matrix optimization via constraint reshaping
abstract: We study quadratic optimization over orthogonality or symplectic constraints, a problem arising in eigenvalue computation, subspace analysis, and reduced-order modeling. Ill-conditioned problems have a wide positive Hessian spectrum at a minimizer, which slows first-order Riemannian methods. Existing preconditioned-metric approaches choose a Riemannian metric, which determines the resulting Hessian spectrum. We instead redesign the problem itself to find the narrowest possible spectrum. We reshape the constraints into equivalent formulations that preserve the optimal value and the solution set, giving a family of preconditioned problems parametrized by positive constraint weights. We derive a closed form for the positive Hessian spectrum in terms of these weights. Minimizing the condition number then reduces to a linear program (LP) in the logarithms of the weights. The LP attains a globally optimal design within the paired equal-block family, and its strong duality gives matching lower bounds on the condition number. On tested instances, the optimized formulation substantially reduces the local condition number, with returned spectra matching predictions on both orthogonal and symplectic instances. We also benchmark the design against Lagrangian and left-right preconditioned metrics. The method thus provides an exact, optimization-based alternative to heuristic preconditioned metrics.

title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
abstract:
Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions.
  In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

title: When Suspicion Adds Up: A Stochastic Framework for Optimizing Honeypot-Based Insider-Threat Detection
abstract: Insider threats pose security risks when employees or other trusted users misuse their access to organizational systems. Detecting these threats is difficult because harmful activity can resemble routine behavior. Honeypots, or decoy resources monitored for suspicious interactions, can provide evidence of potentially malicious activity. We develop a decision framework that models evidence accumulation through honeypot interactions using a continuous-time Markov chain and jointly selects honeypot counts and monitoring horizons to minimize expected losses from malicious activity and false detections. For thresholds of two and three interactions, we derive closed-form true- and false-detection probabilities and expected detection times conditional on detection within the monitoring horizon. We characterize boundary cases and establish stochastic-ordering results. Our numerical results highlight the value of the proposed framework across different settings.

title: Signed QoI Gaps for Goal-Oriented Error Estimation: Reliability and Sharpness from the Same First-Order System Residuals
abstract: There are two common ways to estimate the error in a quantity of interest (QoI). The product of primal and adjoint error estimators gives a reliable but pessimistic bound. The dual-weighted residual method gives a sharp signed estimate from a more accurate approximation of the adjoint solution. We write the primal and adjoint problems as first-order systems and obtain both a reliable bound and a sharp estimate from the same residuals. The first paper of this series (arXiv:2607.23850) uses two consistent evaluators of a quantity of interest, one built from the potentials and one in which the gradients are expressed through the fluxes. We show that they differ exactly by the $A^{-1}$ inner product of the primal and adjoint constitutive residuals, and we call this difference the signed QoI gap. The identity holds for arbitrary primal and adjoint approximations. In our numerical experiments, the signed QoI gap is of the size of the larger of the errors of the two evaluators, while the product of the estimators exceeds this error by factors of up to several hundred. We therefore use the least-squares estimators to refine the mesh and the signed QoI gap to decide when to stop. We also introduce a third evaluator, built from the fluxes alone, which restores the reaction term. The resulting reaction-restored QoI gap estimates the error when reaction dominates. With the non-intrusive least-squares flux recovery, we can apply the method to any discretization that produces a conforming potential, including finite difference and finite volume schemes.

title: Closed $G_2$-structures with fixed metric: compactness and almost-abelian fibres
abstract: We study the space of closed $G_2$-structures inducing a prescribed Riemannian metric and orientation. On a compact seven-manifold, with a fixed Riemannian metric and orientation, we prove that the space of compatible closed $G_2$ structures inducing a prescribed spin-structure is homeomorphic to a real projective algebraic set defined by homogeneous quadratic equations in the kernel of the corresponding Dirac operator. The defining quadrics give a local analytic obstruction map and a Łojasiewicz estimate that bounds the distance to the closed locus in terms of $\|d\varphi\|_{L^2}$. We also prove smooth compactness when the prescribed metrics converge smoothly, and strong $H^1$ compactness for sequences of compatible $G_2$-structures $\varphi_{j}$ satisfying $\|d\varphi_j\|_{L^2}\to 0$. In the invariant setting, the fixed-metric fibre of any seven-dimensional almost-abelian metric Lie algebra has at most four connected components, each a compact homogeneous space. We determine these spaces spectrally when the defining endomorphism is normal, and show that for a non-normal endomorphism the fibre is empty, one circle, or two circles. On compact quotients with symmetric bracket, sufficiently small torus fibres exclude all non-invariant harmonic spinors, so the invariant classification computes the full closed fibre.

title: Rainbow Matchings in $K_{r+1}$-free Graphs
abstract: Let $n,m,r$ be positive integers with $n\ge 2m+2$, where $n$ is sufficiently large relative to $r$. Alon and Frankl determined the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing neither $K_{r+1}$ nor a matching of size $m+1$. In this paper, we establish a rainbow analogue of their result. More precisely, if $G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}$ are $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on a common vertex set of size $n$, each having more than $\operatorname{ex}(n,\{K_{r+1},M_{m+1}\})$ edges, then $\{G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}\}$ admits a rainbow matching.

title: Paper2Lean: Agentic Autoformalization of Mathematical Research Papers at Scale
abstract: Formalizing a mathematical research paper requires more than translating isolated theorems: statements and proofs must remain semantically faithful to the source and globally consistent across long-range dependencies. We introduce Paper2Lean, an end-to-end agentic framework that converts mathematical research papers into integrated Lean projects. The framework extracts mathematical content into a dependency graph and coordinates specialized agents for statement formalization, semantic checking and repair, proof construction, and project integration. We evaluate Paper2Lean on 20 mathematical optimization research papers, using mathlib and a shared library of supporting results. All 20 automatically generated projects compile successfully without proof placeholders. Following human review and semantic repair, we introduce OptPaper-20, a corpus of 20 corrected paper-level formalizations comprising 494 Lean files and 110,910 lines of Lean code. All released projects pass clean builds, with no unresolved discrepancies identified in the audit. These results demonstrate the feasibility of agentic paper-level formalization while highlighting semantic fidelity as a central challenge beyond proof verification. The source code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/TTony2019/OptPaper

title: An asymptotic bound for Yuster's independent transversal factor conjecture
abstract: An $[r,n,1]$-graph has $r$ independent parts of size $n$, with a matching between each pair of parts. Yuster conjectured in 2021 that every such graph has a partition into independent transversals whenever $n\ge 2\lceil r/2\rceil$. We prove that there is an absolute constant $A>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $r$, this partition exists whenever $n\ge\lceil r+A r^{20/21}\rceil$. Thus $f(r)\le r+O(r^{20/21})$, where $f(r)$ is the least $n_0$ such that every $[r,n,1]$-graph has such a partition whenever $n\ge n_0$. In particular, $f(r)/r\to1$, giving an asymptotic form of the conjecture.

title: Matrix-point interpolation for positive real odd functions in one and several variables
abstract: We study the single matrix point interpolation problem for positive real matrix valued functions on the right half-plane, both in the single variable setting and in the noncommutative multivariable setting. In the single variable case, a careful analysis is done for when the solution may or must have a pole at infinity. In the multivariable setting, as the pole structure at infinity can be more complicated, we focus on the case when there is no pole at infinity. The results also yield numerical algorithms for finding a solution.

title: Willmore stability of minimal surfaces in the n-sphere
abstract: We prove that the Lawson minimal surface $ξ_{g,1}$ in $S^3$ is strongly stable for the Willmore bending energy $W$ and remains strongly $W$-stable in $S^n$ for every $n \geq4$; our proof starts with a new lower bound on the area-index of $ξ_{m,k}$ for $m\geq k>1$. Next we observe that each of the $ξ_{m,k}$ and the Karcher-Pinkall-Sterling minimal surfaces in $S^3$, as well as the equilateral minimal torus in $S^5$, is the unique $W$-minimizer in its conformal class, up to Möbius transformations of $S^n$. Finally, we show that although the equilateral minimal torus is $W$-stable in $S^n$ for every $n \geq5$, it is neither strongly $W$-stable nor a local $W$-minimizer: it has a 2-dimensional space of $W$-Jacobi fields on which almost everywhere the third-variation of $W$ is nonzero.

title: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
abstract: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle. First, for a non-exceptional polynomial of degree at least two, we prove that every invariant curve arising from such a semiconjugacy is contained in a generalized circle. Second, in the rational map case, we construct invariant curves arising in this way that are not contained in any generalized circle and have arbitrarily many self-intersections, counted with multiplicity. Moreover, the rational maps can be chosen so that their restrictions to these curves have positive topological entropy.

title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
abstract: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.

title: A variational theory for von Kármán vortex streets
abstract: We construct von Kármán vortex streets as global kinetic energy maximizers for the 2D Euler flow in an infinite periodic channel: our variational framework imposes no a prior symmetry, support constraints, or sign conditions on the admissible class. More specifically, under $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ constraint of the absolute vorticity maximum with other natural constraints, we show that the maximizers are traveling pairs of simply connected vortex patches of support radius $O(\varepsilon)$, converging to the von Kármán point-vortex configuration satisfying glide reflection symmetry as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We prove nonlinear stability of the von Kármán streets under a bound on the vertical support, using a compactness result valid for more general assumptions. Furthermore, we construct slightly tilted asymmetric von Kármán vortex streets as energy maximizers under a tilted moment constraint.

title: The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface
abstract: We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.

title: Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
abstract: For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.

title: Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond
abstract: Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres. Finally, we prove that $I_L$ is unmixed if and only if all its minimal primes have the same height, if and only if the rank of every maximal closed distributive sublattice through an atom of the diamond is $\mathrm{rank}(L)-1$; in this case $I_L$ is radical.

title: Two-Timescale Channel Estimation and Port Selection for Fluid Antenna Systems With Limited Port Observations
abstract: Port selection in fluid antenna systems (FAS) requires instantaneous channel state information, but a single radio-frequency chain can probe only a few ports in each coherence block. Existing FAS channel estimators, even with learned or generative priors, work within a single block and are limited by its few probes, which cannot resolve several propagation paths. To overcome this limitation, we propose a two-timescale channel estimation and port selection scheme that exploits the slow variation of the path angles. Specifically, a sequential Monte Carlo filter accumulates the angle posterior over blocks, while the fast-fading path gains are integrated out in closed form. Furthermore, a Fisher information analysis reveals that a single probe per block carries no angle information, whereas two or more spread-out probes accumulate it linearly over blocks. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme approaches the selection with known angles after about twenty blocks and, with four probes per block, matches memoryless schemes with eight.

title: Feedback-Free FDD Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Sparse AP Activation and Dual-Mode Precoding
abstract: This correspondence enables practical frequency-division duplex (FDD) operation in cell-free massive MIMO via two mechanisms. Sparse access-point (AP) activation reduces downlink pilot overhead to enable coherent detection, while angle-reciprocity precoding steers beams using only uplink-estimated angles, eliminating channel feedback entirely. A load-adaptive dual-mode optimizer further enhances performance: closed-form signal-to-leakage-and-noise-ratio precoding for high-load rate boosting, or semidefinite relaxation for low-load power minimization. Simulations verify its superiority over existing feedback-free FDD solutions in spectral and energy efficiency, and its robustness to angle errors, reciprocity mismatch, and multipath.

title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
abstract: We propose a class of high-order area-preserving Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for the surface diffusion flow of curves, a curvature-driven geometric flow that decreases the perimeter while conserving the enclosed area. By coupling the parametric finite element approximation of the classical BGN formulation with symplectic RK time discretisation, we rigorously prove that the fully discrete scheme unconditionally conserves the enclosed area of curves. This conservation arises solely from the intrinsic symplectic structure of the RK methods, without introducing any additional constraints, auxiliary variables, or Lagrange multipliers to enforce structure preservation. To attain high temporal accuracy, we adopt $q$-stage Gauss RK methods, which are symplectic and yield order $2q$ (e.g., $q=1,2,3$). The resulting fully implicit, strongly nonlinear system is solved efficiently via an equivalent discrete formulation combined with a monolithic damped Newton iteration. Extensive numerical tests on various evolving curves validate the theoretical findings, confirming exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, while the Newton iteration count rapidly decreases to fewer than 8 per step, demonstrating the robustness of the tailored solver.

title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
abstract: Neural networks represent nonlinear process systems accurately, but embedding them in optimization is difficult because smooth activations introduce nonlinear, nonconvex constraints. PWLNet is a Python framework for building optimization-compatible neural surrogates through exact and piecewise-linear reformulations. It combines baseline and physics-informed training, optimization-aware pruning, and Pyomo embeddings based on ReLU mixed-integer linear models, exact tanh nonlinear models, PWL-tanh formulations, and binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP. PWL-native training uses the same activation in training and embedding, avoiding extra linearization error. It is evaluated on Boston housing, the Williams-Otto process, the Van de Vusse reactor, and a hydroformylation semi-batch reactor. On Boston housing, SOSX training gave the best common-architecture model (test MAE 1.984, R2 = 0.925). On Williams-Otto, pruning 15% of hidden neurons reduced MILP solution time 6.5-fold while preserving the selected operating point. For the Van de Vusse reactor, a physics-informed ReLU RNN pruned from 32 to 12 hidden units enabled tractable exact MILP embedding and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy, while terminal-aware shrinking-horizon prediction reached 99.7% of the direct-shooting reference. For the hydroformylation reactor, one-step exact-tanh IPOPT reached 99.2% of the certified reference product with peak pressure 20.002 bar (limit 20 bar) and 14.36 s total solve time over 280 moves; ReLU and PWL-native controllers achieved comparable recovery, with ReLU fastest. Longer horizons and physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results.
