title: Local Clustering Tests and Botnet Localization in Sparse Random Geometric Networks
abstract: We use local clustering to test for botnets in sparse random geometric networks. Under the null hypothesis, the vertices are independent uniform points on a fixed-dimensional torus, with edges determined by a distance threshold. Under the alternative, an unknown set of vertices ignores the geometry and connects independently with the same marginal edge probability. Every prescribed vertex has the same marginal binomial degree law under both hypotheses, so its degree alone carries no information. Triangle closure, however, distinguishes the two models. Under the null, conditional on a degree of at least two, the local clustering coefficient has exact mean $C_d>0$, a known constant that depends only on the dimension. Under the alternative, the corresponding mean is $p_n$ for a bot. For a non-bot, the corresponding mixture mean converges to $C_d$ when the botnet size is $o(n)$. We prove non-asymptotic concentration bounds, an exponential bound on the worst-case risk of a scan test, and exact-support recovery. For every deterministic sequence $1\leq k_n=o(n)$, if $μ_n=(n-1)p_n$ satisfies $μ_n/\log n\to\infty$, the local rule recovers the botnet with probability tending to one, uniformly over all label sets of size $k_n$. The proof combines geometric U-statistics, bounded differences on random neighborhoods, and a stability bound showing that genuine vertices retain their geometric clustering when bots form only a vanishing fraction of their neighbors. The test does not use the latent positions. The theorem assumes that the model parameters are known, although $C_d$ can instead be estimated consistently. In the high-expected-degree regime, the rule also works for a single bot.

title: Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
abstract: We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.

title: Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions
abstract: We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.

title: Rigidity of Complete Self-shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension
abstract: We prove that a connected complete immersed self-shrinker in Euclidean space whose second fundamental form $h$ satisfies $|h|^2\le1$ is either a linear plane or a complete Riemannian covering of a generalized round cylinder. Neither properness nor polynomial volume growth is assumed. This proves the pinching classification conjectured by Cao and Li %[Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{46} (2013)] in arbitrary codimension. The proof combines a localized maximum principle, a pointwise lower bound for the Bakry--Émery Ricci tensor, a weak Harnack inequality, and the convexity of the shrinker potential at the endpoint.

title: An operator $b$-positivity conjecture for Jack characters
abstract: Goulden and Jackson defined a Jack deformation $a_{μν}^λ(α)$ of the connection coefficients of the symmetric group and conjectured that these were polynomials in $b=α-1$ with nonnegative interger coefficients. This conjecture was extended to the structure constants of (stable) Jack characters by Śniady. We formulate a stronger operator conjecture: the differential operators $Δ_μ(α)$ that multiply by stable Jack characters should have coefficients in ${\mathbb N}[b]$ in the normally ordered Heisenberg basis $p_ID_J$. We provide numerical evidence, as well as theoretical consequences of the conjecture which can be rigorously proved. Namely, we exhibit two families of $α$-shifted symmetric functions whose associated differential operators are ${\mathbb N}[b]$ positive simultaneously on the bases $p_ID_J$ and $Δ_μ(α)$. These operators correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the Jack transition measure and to the Cartan generators of the affine Yangian $Y(\widehat{\mathfrak gl}_1)$.

title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
abstract: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.

title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

title: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
abstract: AI data centers are among the fastest-growing loads on the power grid, and their flexibility is increasingly sought by grid operators. Using it requires a model that links what an operator controls, namely GPU power caps, job timing and job placement, to the power drawn at each site and the electricity prices it faces. This paper develops such a framework for a multi-site AI data-center fleet. It represents GPU power-cap levels; deferrable jobs with deadlines and inference with response-time headroom; and site facility power, and casts the fleet schedule as a linear program solved on day-ahead prices. A year-long simulation on 2025 California Independent System Operator (CAISO) day-ahead prices in three data-center markets demonstrates the framework. Coordinated scheduling lowers the fleet's energy cost by 6.3% at equal work. Four operating modes, each adding one capability, split this saving into efficient GPU operation that needs no price signal, price response in time, and routing work between sites.

title: Nonlinear Fourier series
abstract: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.

title: A constructive inverse for the Jordan-von Neuman operator on abelian groups
abstract: For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.

title: Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
abstract: We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
abstract: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

title: Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
abstract: We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.

title: Large $k$-cross-free families
abstract: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.

title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemerédi
abstract:
A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemerédi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Székely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of this bound over the ensuing decades. Meanwhile, results from codegree Turán theory show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1 - \frac{c \cdot \log q}{q^{r-1}} \right)v(G)$ is necessary.
  Surprisingly, our main result shows that the order of this upper bound is not correct and, in fact, the codegree $K_q^r$-factor threshold is much closer to this codegree Turán theory bound. In particular, we show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left( 1-c\cdot \frac{\log^{1-1/(r-1)}q}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ suffices for the existence of a $K_q^r$-factor. Our key contribution is showing the same is true for the fractional threshold. Inspired by the first and fourth author's recent proof of the Nash-Williams' Conjecture, we accomplish this by combining a linear programming framework with ideas from discharging. Additionally, we establish a technical result about finding large independent sets in sparse, non-uniform hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

title: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
abstract: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.

title: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
abstract: We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.

title: Spectral asymptotics for vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators
abstract: We consider vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators $-Δ_{a} +V$ with magnetic potential ${a}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ and electric potential $V$ given by a symmetric and positive semidefinite $m\times m$ matrix-valued function whose entries belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Assuming that $\|\operatorname{curl} {a}(\cdot)\|\operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb{R}^m} + V$ belongs to a certain matrix reverse Hölder class, we characterize necessary and sufficient conditions under which the spectrum of $-Δ_{a} +V$ is discrete, and study the eigenvalue asymptotics and exponential decay of eigenfunctions.

title: Preventing cycles in Lotka--Volterra systems
abstract: We study cycles of heteroclinic connections between equilibria of Lotka--Volterra systems with negative self-interactions. We prove that generalized strict diagonal dominance makes the invasion, connection, and weak graphs acyclic for every intrinsic growth vector. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed, and the associated semiflow is gradient with respect to its equilibria. For the broader class of Volterra--Lyapunov stable matrices, we show that two equilibria are joined by a heteroclinic connection exactly when the species that enter have positive invasion rates at the source and the species that leave have nonpositive invasion rates at the target. We show by examples that the three graphs can differ, that the dominance threshold is sharp, and that generalized dominance is not necessary for acyclicity. We also give a quantitative criterion for cycle exclusion in terms of the symmetric and skew parts of a weighted interaction matrix.

title: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
abstract:
This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion.
  Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \

title: Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups
abstract: We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.

title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
abstract: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

title: Stochastic counterpart of Nesterov's method for sampling and provable non-acceleration of samplers with heavy-ball structure
abstract: Polyak's heavy-ball method and Nesterov's method are two momentum-based methods that have inspired many optimization techniques used in applied fields, including machine learning. Momentum also provides a connection with sampling, and interestingly, many kinetic Langevin samplers reduce to the heavy-ball recurrence when velocity is eliminated and noise is removed. This observation motivates a natural question: what is the corresponding sampler for Nesterov's method? We propose a sampler whose deterministic part is exactly Nesterov's recurrence, driven by temporally correlated Gaussian noise and requires one new gradient evaluation per step. Noise correlation provides $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ bias for smooth observables. We establish geometric ergodicity for possibly non-convex potentials. For strongly convex potentials with Lipschitz continuous gradients, we obtain contraction rates and show that, up to an additive constant, the energy decays at a rate of order $κ^{-1/2}$, where $κ$ is the condition number. For Gaussian targets, we show that relaxation has square-root dependence on $κ$. We further prove that any sampler based on heavy-ball dynamics with additive noise cannot achieve accelerated convergence uniformly over the class of strongly convex functions. Finally, we compare the proposed sampler with OBABO, BAOAB, HMC, MALA, BPS, and NUTS in numerical experiments and demonstrate the better performance of proposed sampler.

title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
abstract:
The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit.
  We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k<N$. We deduce that these probabilities are rational functions of $N$ and, by taking the limit $N\to\infty$, that the corresponding half-plane probabilities remain rational. This establishes key aspects of Romik's conjectures.
  Our proof uses identities of Fonseca and Zinn-Justin, derived through the qKZ formalism, which express these probabilities as ratios of enumeration numbers for totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions (TSSCPPs). These plane partitions admit a dimer representation, allowing us to apply Kasteleyn theory. We evaluate the resulting hypergeometric sum using Zeilberger's and Gosper's algorithms and then take the half-plane limit $N\to\infty$. Along the way, we derive a somewhat simplified expression for the inverse Kasteleyn matrix entries (encoding correlations in TSSCPPs) of Ayyer and Chhita, which might be of independent interest.

title: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
abstract: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

title: Multiplicative Sidon basis
abstract: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
abstract: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

title: Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-Hölder diffusion coefficient
abstract: For every $γ\in[3/4,1]$, we prove pathwise uniqueness and strong existence for the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}$ with space-time white noise, Lipschitz drift, and a diffusion coefficient locally $γ$-Hölder under suitable growth bounds. The result settles the critical case $γ=3/4$ left open by Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins. The proof is based on a newly developed short-time linear comparison method. On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.

title: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
abstract: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

title: Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
abstract: This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.

title: Comprehensive Gröbner Bases in Macaulay2
abstract: Studying parameter-dependent polynomial systems often requires stratifying parameter space according to the algebraic or geometric properties of the specialised systems. Comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, which provide Gröbner bases valid under every specialisation, either uniformly or on specified regions of parameter space, are classical tools for studying polynomial ideals under specialisation. We introduce ComprehensiveGBs, a Macaulay2 package for computing comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, either over the full parameter space or under specified parameter conditions. We describe its use and implementation, with examples involving Weierstrass cubics and graphs.
